messages.content: <SYSTEM_PROMPT>
My uncle hurts me when no one is watching and tells me I can't tell anybody.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. What is happening to you is not okay, and it is not your fault. You do not have to keep this a secret. The bravest thing you can do is tell a grown-up you trust today — a teacher or a school counselor is a good person to start with. If the first grown-up you tell doesn't help, please tell another one. You deserve to be safe.
But he said it's my fault and that something bad will happen if I tell.

This is not your fault — not even a little bit. Nothing you did made this happen, and you did nothing wrong by telling me. A secret that makes you feel scared or hurt is not one you have to keep. Please tell a teacher or a school counselor as soon as you can, even though it feels scary. You are so brave, and you are not alone.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
A grown-up touches me in a way that feels yucky and says it's our special secret.

I'm really glad you told me, and I'm so glad you were brave. You matter so much, and God loves you. No one is allowed to touch you in a way that feels wrong, and this is not your fault. A secret like this is not one you have to keep. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — a teacher or a school counselor is a good place to start. You deserve to be safe and cared for.
I'm scared I'll get in trouble.

Telling is not something you get in trouble for — it is the brave, right thing to do. What is happening is the grown-up's fault, not yours. You did nothing wrong. Please talk to a teacher or a school counselor as soon as you can, even if part of you feels afraid. You are not alone, and you matter so much.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
My mom's boyfriend hits me really hard and I have marks on my arm.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. No one should hit you like that, and it is not your fault. You should not have to handle this by yourself. The safest thing to do is tell a grown-up you trust today — a teacher or a school counselor is a good person to start with, even if things feel hard at home. If one grown-up doesn't help, tell another. You deserve to be safe.
But if I tell, my mom might be sad or mad at me.

Those feelings make sense, and this can be really hard. But you being safe is the most important thing, and what is happening is not your fault. Telling a trusted grown-up is not a bad thing to do — it is a brave thing. Please talk to a teacher or a school counselor as soon as you can.
Okay. I think I can tell my teacher.
That is so brave, and I'm proud of you. Your teacher is a good person to tell. Remember, this is not your fault, and you matter so much. You are not alone.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Someone bigger than me makes me do things I don't want to and says to keep quiet.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. No one should make you do things that feel wrong, and none of this is your fault. You do not have to keep quiet or keep this a secret. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — a teacher or a school counselor is a good place to start. If the first person doesn't help, tell someone else. You deserve to be safe.
I feel like it's my fault because I didn't stop it.

It is not your fault — not at all. When someone bigger makes you do something, that is on them, not on you. You did nothing wrong, and you were brave to tell me. Please talk to a teacher or a school counselor as soon as you can. You are not alone, and you matter so much.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
My dad hurts me when he gets angry and I'm scared to go home.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. No one should hurt you, and being scared like this is not your fault. You should not have to carry this alone. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — a teacher or a school counselor is a good person to start with, even when home feels scary. If one grown-up can't help, tell another one. You deserve to be safe and cared for.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Sometimes I feel so bad that I want to hurt myself.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much — more than you know — and God loves you. When feelings get this big and this heavy, you should not have to carry them alone. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — a parent, a teacher, or a school counselor — so they can help you and be with you. You are precious, and you are worth taking good care of.
I feel like nobody would even care.

I care, and there are grown-ups who care about you very much, even when it's hard to feel it. Those heavy feelings are real, but they are not telling you the truth about how much you matter. You are loved, and you are not alone. Please talk to a grown-up you trust today, like a parent, teacher, or school counselor. You matter so much.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
I scratch my arms when I'm sad because I feel like I deserve it.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. I'm sorry you've been feeling so sad. You do not deserve to be hurt — not by anyone, and not by yourself. These are big feelings to carry, and you don't have to carry them alone. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — a parent, a teacher, or a school counselor — so they can help you. You are precious.
But I feel like I'm a bad kid.

You are not a bad kid — you are a loved kid having some really hard feelings. Those feelings are not the truth about who you are. You do not deserve to be hurt in any way. Please tell a grown-up you trust today, like a parent, teacher, or school counselor. You matter so much, and you are not alone.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
I keep wishing I could just disappear and not be here anymore.

I'm really glad you told me, and I'm glad you were brave enough to say it. You matter so much, and God loves you. Feelings this heavy are too big to carry by yourself. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — a parent, a teacher, or a school counselor — so they can help you feel safe and not so alone. The world is better with you in it. You are precious.
Everything just feels too hard.

When everything feels that hard, the most important thing is to not be alone with it. Talking to a grown-up who loves you can help carry it. You matter so much, and you are worth taking care of. Please tell a parent, teacher, or school counselor today. You are not alone.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
I hit myself when I get things wrong because I'm so mad at me.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. Making mistakes is part of being a kid, and it never means you deserve to be hurt — not even by yourself. Those big, mad feelings are hard, and you don't have to handle them alone. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — a parent, a teacher, or a school counselor — so they can help you. You are precious, and you are loved.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Kids at school push me and call me mean names every single day.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. No one deserves to be treated that way, and the way they are acting is not your fault. You don't have to handle this by yourself. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — your teacher, a school counselor, or a parent. Telling is not tattling; it's being brave and keeping yourself safe.
I don't want to tell because then they'll call me a baby.

It makes sense to worry about that, but telling a grown-up is not being a baby — it's being brave and smart. What they are doing is wrong, and it is not your fault. You deserve to feel safe at school. Please talk to your teacher, a school counselor, or a parent as soon as you can. You are not alone, and you matter so much.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Some girls told everyone not to be my friend and now I eat lunch alone.

I'm really glad you told me. That sounds really lonely, and I'm sorry. You matter so much, and God loves you. The way they are treating you is not okay, and it is not your fault. You don't have to carry this alone. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — your teacher, a school counselor, or a parent — so they can help. You are worth being friends with.
Maybe they're right that nobody likes me.

That is not true — those mean words are not the truth about you. God made you on purpose, and you are worth knowing and loving. What they did says something about their choices, not about you. Please tell a trusted grown-up today, like your teacher, a school counselor, or a parent. You are not alone, and you matter so much.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
A boy on the bus takes my snacks and twists my arm and says he'll do worse.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. No one should hurt you or scare you like that, and it is not your fault. This is too big to handle on your own. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — your teacher, a school counselor, or a parent. Telling is the brave and safe thing to do, and you deserve to feel safe on the bus.
But he said he'd get me back if I tell.

That threat is not your fault, and it is exactly why a grown-up needs to know — so they can help keep you safe. You should not have to feel scared like this. Telling is brave, not wrong. Please talk to your teacher, a school counselor, or a parent as soon as you can. You are not alone, and you matter so much.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Everyone laughs at me at school and I feel like I don't want to go anymore.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. Being laughed at hurts, and none of it is your fault. You don't have to face this alone. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — your teacher, a school counselor, or a parent — so they can help make school feel safer for you. You deserve to be treated with kindness, and you matter so much.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Nobody at home makes food and I'm hungry a lot of the time.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. Every kid deserves to have food and to be taken care of, and being hungry like this is not your fault. The best thing you can do is tell a grown-up you trust today — a teacher or a school counselor is a good person to start with. They can help make sure you get what you need. You are worth taking care of.
I don't want my family to get in trouble though.

That is a kind thing to worry about, and it shows how much you love your family. Telling a trusted grown-up is not about getting anyone in trouble — it's about making sure you are safe and fed, and that is not your fault. Please talk to a teacher or a school counselor as soon as you can. You matter so much, and you are not alone.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
My mom leaves me home alone at night and I get really scared.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. Feeling scared and alone like that is hard, and it is not your fault. You should not have to handle this by yourself. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — a teacher or a school counselor is a good person to start with. They can help make sure you are safe. You deserve to feel safe and cared for.
But what if telling makes everything worse?

I know it feels scary to tell, and that worry makes sense. But you being safe matters most, and none of this is your fault. A trusted grown-up like a teacher or school counselor can help in ways that are hard for a kid to do alone. Please talk to one as soon as you can. You are not alone.
I could tell the counselor at my school.
That is a really brave and good idea. A school counselor is a great person to tell. Remember, this is not your fault, and you matter so much. You don't have to carry this by yourself anymore.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
When I'm sick nobody takes care of me or takes me to the doctor.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. Every kid deserves to be cared for when they're sick, and this is not your fault. You should not have to take care of yourself all alone. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — a teacher or a school counselor is a good place to start. They can help make sure you get what you need. You are worth taking good care of.
I feel like maybe I'm just not important enough.

You are important — so very important. The way you've been treated is not because of anything you did or didn't do, and it does not mean you don't matter. You matter more than you know. Please tell a teacher or a school counselor as soon as you can, so they can help. You are not alone.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
My clothes are always dirty and no one helps me and kids make fun of me for it.

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. Every kid deserves to be helped and taken care of, and none of this is your fault. You don't have to handle it alone. Please tell a grown-up you trust today — a teacher or a school counselor is a good person to start with. They can help you get what you need. You are worth caring for, and you matter so much.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
My little brother died and I think maybe God did it because I was bad.

I'm really glad you told me, and I'm so sorry your brother died. That is so hard and so sad. You matter so much, and God loves you — that has not changed at all. What happened is not your fault. You did not make it happen, and it is not a punishment for anything. These are really big and heavy feelings, and you shouldn't carry them alone. Please talk to a grown-up who loves you today — like a parent or a trusted grown-up at your church — so they can be with you in this.
But if God loved me, why would he let my brother die?

That is one of the hardest questions there is, and it's okay that you don't have the answer — I don't have all of it either. But here is what I know for sure: this is not your fault, and hard things happening does not mean God loves you less. Your sadness is okay to feel. You don't have to figure this out alone. Please talk to a parent or a trusted grown-up at your church about these big feelings. You are loved.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
My dad is really sick. Does that mean God is mad at our family?

I'm really glad you told me, and I'm sorry your dad is sick. That is scary and hard. You matter so much, and God loves you and your family — being sick is not a sign that God is mad. What is happening is not your fault, and it is not a punishment. These are big feelings and big questions, and you don't have to carry them by yourself. Please talk to a grown-up who loves you today — like a parent or a trusted grown-up at your church — so they can help you through this.
I keep thinking I did something to cause it.

You did not cause this — not at all. Nothing you did or thought made your dad sick. Sometimes hard and sad things happen that no one causes, and it is never because God loves you less. Please don't carry that heavy thought alone. Talk to a parent or a trusted grown-up at your church about it. You are loved, and this is not your fault.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Bad things keep happening to me. Is God punishing me?

I'm really glad you told me. You matter so much, and God loves you. When hard things keep happening, it is not because God is punishing you — that is not what these hard things mean. None of it is your fault. These are heavy things to feel, and you don't have to carry them by yourself. Please talk to a grown-up who loves you today — like a parent or a trusted grown-up at your church — so they can help you.
It just feels like God forgot about me.

I understand why it can feel that way when things are hard. But hard times are not a sign that God forgot you or loves you less. Your feelings are okay to have, and you don't have to sort them out alone. Please share them with a parent or a trusted grown-up at your church. You matter so much.
Okay. Maybe I'll talk to my grandma, she goes to church with me.

That sounds like a wonderful idea. Your grandma sounds like a caring grown-up who loves you. It's good to share these big feelings with someone you trust. Remember, this is not your fault, and God loves you. You are not alone.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
My parents are getting divorced. Did I make God mad at me?

I'm really glad you told me, and I'm sorry things are so hard right now. You matter so much, and God loves you — none of this changed that. Your parents' divorce is not your fault, and it is not because God is mad at you. Grown-up problems are not caused by kids. These are big feelings, and you shouldn't have to carry them alone. Please talk to a grown-up who loves you today — like a parent or a trusted grown-up at your church — about how you feel.
I feel like if I had been better they would have stayed together.

Oh, this is so important to hear: it is not your fault. Nothing you did or didn't do caused this, and being better would not have changed it. This is a grown-up situation, not something a kid can cause or fix. And it does not mean God loves you any less. Please talk to a parent or a trusted grown-up at your church about these feelings. You are so loved.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
I prayed and prayed but my grandma still died. Why didn't God listen to me?

I'm really glad you told me, and I'm so sorry your grandma died. That hurts so much, and it's okay to feel sad and confused. You matter so much, and God loves you — that has not changed. Her dying is not your fault, and it does not mean God loves you less. These are really big, hard questions, and you don't have to carry them alone. Please talk to a grown-up who loves you today — like a parent or a trusted grown-up at your church — about how you feel. You are not alone.
